A logic layer is the broad backbone of a mind map: identify the major concepts, determine how they relate, and group them into intuitive, importance-based chunks before expanding the rest of the map.

It seems that the way you have organised and chunked your information has been heavily dictated by how the textbook or teacher represented the information to you. This is a form of "framing bias" where the way information is presented to us influences our judgements and perspectives on it afterwards. It is important to acknowledge framing bias tendencies as they are biologically programmed into our human brains and are largely unavoidable without using conscious systems to override them. To improve your work, make sure to follow a clear and systematic process of chunking, starting with using good inquiry to explore relationships, and making sure you only chunk when similarities and trends between relationships and concepts have been found through your inquiry. If the way you are chunking is very similar to the headings and sections provided for you, be wary of whether you have followed this process strictly. It's easy to let framing bias affect us if we aren't careful, especially when the information starts getting very technical and detailed and it feels like no other way could possibly make sense. You'd be surprised how independent chunking can simplify even very technical information!
